rationale: Compilation now correctly implements the corrected design: the focal selector (user_teams → users → messages → channels → channel_members, filtered on channel_members.user_id = 'U_INCOGNITO') faithfully encodes 'authors who posted in the same channel Carlos belongs to,' and mechanical_checks reports zero errors with computed_matches exactly {Priya, Mateo, Kenji} matching the card's Referent set and the private expected_matches — confirming the prior O1 entity-naming defect is fully resolved (target roles/bindings now key on user_teams rows, not bare user identities). Base-seed facts support every claim: Carlos (U_INCOGNITO) has exactly one channel_members row (C_GROWTH), the three matched authors each have exactly one user_teams row with role 'member,' and the three near-miss negatives (Łukasz — member of C_GROWTH but never posts there; Carlos himself — member with no messages; Robert Walsh — admin role but only posts in #general) are all verified against the message/channel_members seed rows and correctly excluded from the join. Answer_attributes (user_teams.role/user_id/team_id) are bare, real columns matching the schema, and Identifying paths list only entity/edge sequences as required. The one seed_edit — granting the actor a channel_members row in product-growth — is a reasonable, narrowly justified access grant for conversations.history discovery of a channel the actor wasn't previously in, and it does not alter any referent, match, or negative record, so it satisfies the 'no change to intended referents' constraint. Access plan (conversations.members/history + users.info against user_teams) is realistic given the documented API surface and the single-workspace-per-user setup noted in runtime_qualifications. The prompt is a concise, ordinary read question with well-differentiated negatives and no unsupported operations, yielding a strong-quality, fully valid case.
